grades.quote: Now that sleep holds just p->lock, it can put the process to sleep by recording the wait channel, changing the process state to SLEEPING, and calling sched (2718-2721). In a moment it will be clear why it’s critical that p->lock is not released (by scheduler) until after the process is marked SLEEPING.
grades.reason: Explains the sleep/wakeup locking rationale and holding p->lock into sched, but only partially addresses why lock ownership transfers across swtch.
